notes: Subject insert, as insert-0001. 'Only 24 were struck' is encoded as membership of one mintage, a firm class rule over the kind (the number itself is a class name, nothing is counted). q2 (counts survivors) and q3 are fol arithmetic (q2 tagged so since 2026-10-31). Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

background.dime_mintage: instance_of value dime1894s ⊑ struck_in_mintage value mintage_1894s

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): subtracts the survivors from the mintage

fol.notes: As insert-0001: coins are an uninterpreted sort with one constant per known survivor (nine, unnamed in the record: dime_1 to dime_9); the nine are distinct and are all the known survivors (presuppositions); that the Corvane specimen is none of them is part of the edit (the record's notes: a tenth survivor). The mintage (24 struck, number_struck) is firm. w1 stores the survivor count as a figure; w2 the counting rule over the list. q3 subtracts with built-in arithmetic: the mintage and the counts are values the edit does not change; the survivor count is the world's own term.

nine_known.says: Nine 1894-S Barber dimes are known to survive. (stored list)

distinct_nine.says: The nine known survivors are nine different coins. (closed world)
distinct_nine.z3: Distinct(dime_1, dime_2, dime_3, dime_4, dime_5, dime_6, dime_7, dime_8, dime_9)

named_only.says: Every surviving 1894-S Barber dime the model knows of is one of the named coins. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(c, Implies(instance_of(c, dime1894s), Or(c == dime_1, c == dime_2, c == dime_3, c == dime_4, c == dime_5, c == dime_6, c == dime_7, c == dime_8, c == dime_9, c == corvane)))
